"description": "This is a USA EST Role, you must be able to work within our hours for at least 4 hours a day. 

We are an established automotive e-commerce company looking for an experienced Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) Specialist to take ownership of improving conversion across our entire customer journey.

This is not a graphic design position.

This is not a position where you simply audit our website, give us 50 recommendations, and disappear.

We're looking for someone who continuously asks:

Where are customers dropping off? Why is it happening? What does the data tell us? What should we test? And did the experiment actually make the business more money?

You will work directly with our CEO (who is a coder himself) and development team. We can implement changes quickly.

Your primary responsibility is figuring out WHAT deserves to be improved, WHY, what we should TEST, and whether it actually WORKED.

What You'll Own

You will analyze and optimize the complete e-commerce journey:

Traffic → Search/Vehicle Selection → Category → Product → Add to Cart → Cart → Checkout → Purchase → Repeat Customer

Your responsibilities may include:

Analyze GA4 and customer behavior data
Review Microsoft Clarity/session recordings
Identify major funnel drop-offs
Analyze mobile vs. desktop conversion
Analyze conversion by traffic source and landing page
Investigate product discovery and search behavior
Identify PDP conversion opportunities
Identify cart and checkout friction
Identify opportunities to increase AOV
Identify opportunities to increase repeat purchases
Analyze new vs. returning customers
Analyze different customer segments
Develop hypotheses supported by evidence
Prioritize opportunities based on expected business impact
Maintain a prioritized experimentation backlog
Design A/B tests
Define primary and guardrail metrics before launching tests
Create clear experiment requirements for developers
QA experiments before launch
Analyze experiment results
Document wins, losses, and learnings
Continuously determine what we should test next

We don't want someone focused on only one page.

You own finding conversion opportunities across the entire customer journey.

How We Think About CRO

We don't want:

"I think this page would look better if..."

We want:

Data → Problem → Hypothesis → Experiment → Measurement → Learning → Next Experiment

For example:

Not:

"The PDP needs a redesign."

Instead:

"Mobile visitors without confirmed vehicle fitment convert significantly worse. Session behavior suggests uncertainty around compatibility. I recommend testing X. Here is the evidence, hypothesis, primary metric, guardrails, and engineering requirement."

Our developers can then implement the experiment.

You measure what happens.

If it wins, great.

If it loses, that's okay too.

We want someone who learns from the result rather than trying to prove every idea was correct.

What We Measure

We care about business outcomes such as:

Conversion Rate
Revenue Per Visitor / Session
Gross Profit or Contribution Per Visitor
Add-to-Cart Rate
Checkout Completion Rate
Average Order Value
Repeat Purchase Rate
Customer Lifetime Value

Increasing conversion while destroying AOV or profitability is not necessarily a win.

We want someone who understands the economics behind the metrics.

Required Experience

We're looking for someone with strong hands-on experience in:

E-commerce Conversion Rate Optimization
A/B Testing
GA4
Funnel Analysis
Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar, FullStory, or similar tools
Behavioral Analysis
Experiment Design
Statistical Analysis / Significance
Product Page Optimization
Cart & Checkout Optimization
Mobile Conversion Optimization
Data Analysis

You should be comfortable working directly with developers and turning your hypotheses into clear implementation requirements.

Strongly Preferred

Experience with:

Large-catalog e-commerce
Technical products
Automotive
Electronics
Industrial products
Hardware
Parts
Marketplaces
Google Tag Manager
PostHog
Customer research
Lifecycle/retention optimization
Basic HTML/CSS/JavaScript understanding
AI Experience

Experience using tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, or other AI tools is a plus.

You do not need to be a software engineer.

We care much more about finding someone with exceptional CRO judgment, analytical ability, and commercial thinking.

Our technical team can implement your ideas.

About AutoBuffy

AutoBuffy is an automotive e-commerce company selling aftermarket automotive parts across a large catalog.

Automotive e-commerce presents an interesting conversion challenge:

Customers aren't simply deciding whether they like a product.

They need confidence that they're purchasing the correct part for their specific vehicle and repair.

Our long-term goal is to make buying automotive parts remarkably simple, accurate, informative, and trustworthy.

We already have meaningful traffic and sales.

Your job is to help us generate more profitable customers from the traffic and opportunities we already have.

Hours & Relationship

We expect to begin around 15–20 hours per week.

This is intended to be a long-term relationship, and the role can grow based on performance and business needs.

We care more about the quality of your thinking and results than simply filling hours.

Individual Applicants Only — No Agencies

We are looking for an individual CRO professional who wants to become deeply familiar with one e-commerce business.

No agencies.

If you operate an agency or intend to delegate the work to other people, please do not apply.

title: Operations Manager For Digital Agency
description:
Comet Fuel is hiring for an Operations Manager!

Qualified candidates will be sent the full role details.

🚀 Have you led a team where holding the standard was YOUR job, not something you escalated up?

🚀 Do you naturally think in systems - seeing repetitive work and recurring problems as design flaws you can't help but map, fix, and eliminate?

🚀 Have you lived somewhere in the marketing, ads, or agency world, so "the client's CPL doubled" is a sentence you understand, not one you need translated?

🚀 Can you have the direct, courageous conversation without spending three days rehearsing it (or resenting having to have it)?

🚀 Do you get more satisfaction from your TEAM's wins than from your own headline projects?

🚀 Are you looking to help build the map at a small, growing company - not be handed one at a big, polished one?

If you answered "yes!" to all of the above, you might be our next Operations Manager! 


What we’re offering:
⭐ $35-$50/hr ($72,800-$104,000/year at full-time). W2 or 1099 available.
⭐100% remote. You should generally be available during EST daytime hours, M-F
⭐Part-time to Full-time: To start, we expect 15-20 hours a week, growing to 25-30 once you’re fully onboarded and integrated into our team, culture, processes, and strategy. As we grow, we’ll be looking to expand this to full-time.
⭐This position is only open to US citizens. You must reside in EST, CST, MST, or PST timezone.
⭐ Start date is as soon as possible.

The role’s objective: 
You will own the engine of the business: leading and developing a team that solves problems; running and optimizing for world-class systems and infrastructure that keeps delivery consistent without founder involvement; and commanding unparalleled service quality so client retention stays high and escalations to Jarod become rare events. You are the layer that turns his strategy and R&D into strategic, executed, and repeatable operations that drive progressive results.

Your success looks like a team that stays together and grows better together, clients who stay and spend more (because they’re making more), processes that are 100% documented and actually followed because you build and train in a way that gives the team leverage, and a founder whose calendar is finally full of the work only he can do.

Primary responsibilities
👉 Protect the founder’s focus - You're the filter between our founder and the noise. Fires route through you first.
👉 Lead & manage the team - You run the 1:1s, hold the standards, develop the people, and own both team and client retention.
👉 Oversee daily operations - You keep the day running on rails.
👉 Systems & process ownership - You’re the systems architect, designing solutions that fix recurring problems and owning whether it works or not.
👉 Client support & Escalations - You become the first point of escalation (after our team) so an issue reaching the founder becomes a rare event.
👉 Govern file system 0rganization - You set & manage the rules that keep Google Drive and ClickUp so clean that anyone can find anything in under a minute
👉 Maintain inbox-zero daily - Email, ClickUp, and Slack hit zero before you sign off.
👉 Govern project management - You govern ClickUp as the single source of truth, so anyone can open it and know what's happening, who owns it, and what's next, without asking a human.

Must have experience with:
👉 Operations management. You've owned and empowered teams, processes, systems, and outcomes, not just tasks or projects.
👉 You’ve held a role requiring de-escalation. You've handled frustrated or angry people and you're naturally good at it.
👉 2+ years using ClickUp (or comparable PM software)
👉 2+ years of high-performance remote work.
👉 2+ Years of marketing, agency, or ads-adjacent experience. You DO NOT need to be a marketer. You do need to know enough that client conversations, campaign concepts, and agency rhythms are familiar ground.
👉 You've worked somewhere small (under $3M) that grew considerably ($20M+).

About Comet Fuel
Comet Fuel’s mission is to empower founders to sustainably grow to $5M-$10M/yr through holistic & measurable advertising campaigns (without all the typical agency BS).

—

title: Logo Designer for Marine Science & Exploration Research Team
description:
We are a marine science research team looking for a designer to create a distinctive logo for our group. Our work focuses on coral reefs and fishes, particularly the exploration of deeper, poorly known mesophotic (“twilight zone”) reefs around the world.

We’re looking for a logo that combines science, ocean exploration, diving, and discovery. We particularly like the aesthetic of modern scientific badge/emblem logos and expedition patches, with simple flat-vector or monoline illustrations, bold typography, and a slightly organic feel.

We would like something contemporary and clean, but with personality—more like an exploration or expedition identity than a corporate or institutional logo. Possible visual elements could include reef fishes, a deep reef or reef wall, a technical diver, depth/light gradients, or other imagery suggesting exploration of the ocean’s twilight zone. We have some ideas, but we want the designer to bring their own creativity to the project.

The logo will be used on social media, presentations, expedition materials, stickers, shirts, hats, and potentially dive gear, so it should work well both digitally and in print.

We are looking for a designer with strong experience in logo design, illustration, and visual identity. Experience with science, nature, diving, outdoor, or exploration-related brands is a plus.

The project should include several initial concepts, refinement of the selected direction, and final logo files in full-color and monochrome versions, including vector files.

When applying, please share examples of original logos you have designed, particularly badge/emblem, expedition, outdoor, nature, or science-related designs.
